summary: Yudru Tsomu is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp, Mark Elliott, Janet Gyatso, and Philip A. Kuhn, having also studied under James E. Bosson, Wesley M. Jacobsen, and Kent Buys.

Yuen Ren Chao was a linguist and sinologist who studied at Tsinghua (~1910), Cornell (1910–1914), and Harvard (1915–1918). He held posts at Cornell (~1919–1920), Harvard (~1921–1924), Tsinghua (~1925–1929), and the University of California, Berkeley (~1947–1963).
Yuexia was a scholar in Buddhist studies who founded Huayan University and served there as a teacher.

Yuguang Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 under Bsam gtan, Tashi Tsering, Gongbaojie, and Gyalog, and earned a PhD from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2005).
Yuhiko Katsuzaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1965–1974) and later served there as university president (~2011–2015).
Yui Chi Lau was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ying-Kuang Chu and founded the Hong Kong Vajrayana Esoteric Society.

Yui Suzuki is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology who earned a degree at the University of California, Los Angeles, under William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum. Suzuki was attested at the University of Maryland, College Park in 2012.

Yuichi Kajiyama (1925–2004) was a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology scholar. Educated at Kyoto University, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, SOAS, and Vienna, he held faculty posts at Kyoto University (1956–1988), Bukkyo University (1988–1997), and Soka University (1997–2001).
Yuichi Shionoya was a scholar of philosophy and other fields who studied at Nagoya University (~1950–1953) and Hitotsubashi University (~1953–1958). He held a post at Nagoya University (~1961–1967).

Yuishin Ito was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who studied at Bukkyo University and Doshisha University. He taught at Bukkyo University from 1961 (becoming professor emeritus 1974–1997) and served as president of Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College in 1997.

Yujiro Motora was a scholar of philosophy and other fields who studied at Johns Hopkins University in 1885. He held appointments at Tokyo University of Education (~1888) and the University of Tokyo (~1888–1912).

Yujun Endo was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held appointments at Taisho University, where he was an associate professor (attested 1991) and professor emeritus (attested 2014), and served as an advisor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).
Yuka Otani is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held posts as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University and Hanazono University (both attested 2015).
Yukari Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under doctoral supervisor Kenyu Mitomo. Kimura held a post at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).

Yukei Matsunaga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Koyasan University, Tohoku University, and Kyushu University. He held positions at Shuchiin University and served as director at Koyasan University in 1983.

Yuki Kyogoku is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who worked at Accenture (2013–2014). Kyogoku served as a research associate at the University of Leipzig in 2018, where he was also a doctoral student (attested 2026).

Yuki Sasaki is a scholar of history/archaeology and Buddhist studies who held posts as a part-time lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (both attested 2026).
Yuki Shibuya is a scholar of sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned a Ph.D. at the University of Tokyo (2016–2018), where Shibuya was also a project research fellow in 2014.
Yuki Takatsukasa is a scholar in Buddhist studies who pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015) and later served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2017).

Yukihiko Asayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who served as a professor at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and as a Ministry of Education overseas researcher at South China Normal University (attested 1991).
